# aot-warning-baseline — the committed record of what the NativeAOT publish of
# apps/Harbor.App.Cli actually does, as measured by the `aot-publish` job.
#
# OWNER: issue #413. Read by tools/aot-publish-gate.py on every PR. This is a
# RATCHET, not a target: the gate passes only when the publish's outcome and its
# diagnostics are exactly what is written here, and a change in EITHER direction
# is red.
#
# ── THE HEADLINE, SO NOBODY HAS TO RUN THE GATE TO LEARN IT ────────────────
#
#   THE AOT PUBLISH PUBLISHES (recipe `fulltree`). This is measured, not predicted.
#
#     recipe `fulltree` (-p:HarborWithAot=true) — reaches ILC and completes
#       (HARBOR_AOT_PUBLISH_DONE rid=linux-x64 recipe=fulltree status=published
#       exit=0, first measured on the #1055 slice-3 branch, CI run 38035398971).
#       The IL3000/IL2070/IL2072 errors left with the in-process plugin
#       pipeline: #1055s3 removed the CLI's references to
#       Harbor.Plugins.{Storage,Compilation,Instantiation,Registration}, so
#       Roslyn (Microsoft.CodeAnalysis) and the reflection instantiator are no
#       longer in the trim graph. No suppression was added — the four demoted
#       warning ids below are all that remains, which satisfies #413's "no
#       blanket suppression" criterion structurally rather than textually.
#
#     recipe `minimal` (HARBOR_MINIMAL=true, the stripped profile the csproj
#       calls the real AOT path) — not evaluated by this gate and unchanged by
#       this record: it does not compile (11 x CS0234, PluginReloadService.cs
#       inside `#if HARBOR_WITH_PLUGINS` with unguarded call sites). #1055s3
#       kept the guard and the call-site shape, so that state is carried over,
#       not re-triaged here.
#
#   The gate publishes `fulltree`. The rows below are what it emits.
#
#   CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ARTIFACT CHECK: the "run the published binary" half is
#   LIVE as of this record. A `published` outcome must produce an executable
#   that runs --version/--help/--providers on content; the smoke step asserts
#   both directions, so a future failure that stops emitting the binary goes
#   red there first. Do not read a green job as a claim that Harbor is
#   AOT-clean — only that the publish completes and the artifact boots.
#
# ── WHY THE OLD ERROR ROWS ARE GONE ─────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The three REJECTED error ids (IL3000 x4, IL2072, IL2070) are deleted by this
# record, not demoted: the code that emitted them no longer ships in the CLI
# process. #413 forbade buying green with blanket suppression, and none was
# bought — the Roslyn IL3000 inside Microsoft.CodeAnalysis itself is gone
# because Roslyn is gone from this binary (it lives in harbor-plugins-host,
# a JIT process), and the instantiator annotations are moot for the same
# reason. Deleting the rows is the transition the gate exists to force, and
# this file is where it is acknowledged.
#
# ── FORMAT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   ID | severity | count | verdict | first-party sites | reason
#
#   ID        IL2xxx (trim), IL3xxx (AOT), or CS (in scope only because the
#             stripped recipe currently fails to compile). One row per
#             (id, severity): the same id as a warning and as an error are two
#             different rows, or an error could hide behind a warning's count.
#   severity  warning | error. A demoted warning still has to be accounted for;
#             an error is the reason the publish fails.
#   count     exact occurrences. A change in EITHER direction fails.
#   verdict   ACCEPTED = a concession this repository carries, with the reason in
#                       the last field. Expected to keep appearing.
#             REJECTED = a defect that ought to be fixed. ALSO expected to keep
#                       appearing — that is the point: when one stops appearing
#                       the gate goes red and the row has to be promoted or
#                       deleted, so a fix cannot land unrecorded.
#   sites     '-' when every site is third-party; else the comma-separated
#             first-party SITES. A "site" is the Harbor TYPE the diagnostic
#             names, not a file path: ILC and ILLink print a symbol and no
#             source file, and the only real path in an ILC log is Roslyn's own
#             src/Compilers/... which is third-party. A new site fails even at an
#             unchanged count. A site MAY include a method name where the tool
#             named one; it is not trimmed off, because the two line shapes are
#             indistinguishable (ILC writes `Type.Method(args):` where a
#             compiler line writes `Type(line,col):`) and trimming wrong records
#             a site that does not exist. Line numbers are absent on purpose —
#             they move on every unrelated edit.
#   reason    >= 40 characters, not a bare URL — the same floor and URL rule
#             tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/ExemptionReason.cs applies to
#             every other table in this repo, so there is one definition of
#             "states a reason".
#
# ── COUNTS ARE PINNED AGAINST A FLOATING SDK ───────────────────────────────
#
# `actions/setup-dotnet` is given `10.0.x`, so a new 10.0 patch can change the
# analyzer set and therefore these counts. That is intentional: a new trim
# warning is real information and the gate must be able to go red about it. The
# cost is that an SDK bump may need this file re-triaged in the same diff.
#
# ── CROSS-CHECK, AND AN ASYMMETRY THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING ───────────────
#
# tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/AotBlockDemotionRules.cs asserts that the ids
# here and the ids Harbor.App.Cli.csproj's WarningsNotAsErrors demotes name the
# same set. They now DO: the csproj demotes four (IL2026, IL3050, IL2104,
# IL3053) and the publish emits exactly those four as warnings, with no error
# rows left. The asymmetry #413 recorded (three REJECTED error ids the csproj
# did not cover) resolved when #1055s3 moved the plugin compile pipeline out
# of the CLI process.

IL2026 | warning | 8 | ACCEPTED | Harbor.Hosting.Configuration.ImmutableDictionaryConverter, Harbor.Hosting.Configuration.ImmutableListConverter, Harbor.Ipc.Protocol.HarborRequestTypes.BuildCensus, Harbor.Providers.OpenAiCompatible.ProviderConfig, Harbor.Storage.Jsonl.JsonlMessageCodec.DeserializePart | Demoted by the csproj through WarningsNotAsErrors, so these print and do not fail the publish. #1055s3 removed the six plugin-pipeline occurrences (CollectiblePluginLoadContext LoadFromImage and LoadFromPluginPath, FindPluginTypes, FileTrustPolicy and PersistAccept); what remains is reflection-based JSON plus one GetTypes census. The JsonSerializerContext work is real but is convention rather than a rule, per the block's own comment.

IL3050 | warning | 7 | ACCEPTED | Harbor.Hosting.Configuration.ImmutableDictionaryConverter, Harbor.Hosting.Configuration.ImmutableListConverter, Harbor.Providers.OpenAiCompatible.ProviderConfig, Harbor.Storage.Jsonl.JsonlMessageCodec.DeserializePart | Demoted by the csproj. JsonSerializer.Deserialize and Serialize of T without a source-generated context. #1055s3 removed the FileTrustPolicy pair along with the Roslyn RequiresDynamicCode source; the remainder is the JSON-convention cleanup, no longer owned by #48/S4.

IL2104 | warning | 2 | ACCEPTED | - | Per-assembly trim rollup inside referenced packages: MessagePack and MemoryPack.Core. #1055s3 dropped Microsoft.CodeAnalysis from the published graph, so its rollup is gone. Demoted by the csproj. Third-party internals, so there is no first-party site to triage; see the IL2026 row for our half.

IL3053 | warning | 2 | ACCEPTED | - | Per-assembly AOT rollup for MessagePack and MemoryPack.Core. Unchanged by #1055s3. The csproj records this id as UNIDENTIFIED, carried since before #747 and not matched to a documented diagnostic from this checkout. This publish is further evidence that it is a real per-assembly AOT rollup, but the identification is not confirmed, so the row stays ACCEPTED rather than being promoted on a guess.
